Name: Sankofa Pendant Necklace
Short description: A pendant for the symbol that means going back for what matters.
Description:
Sankofa — Go back and fetch it. Carry where you come from into where you're going.

The Sankofa bird flies forward with its head turned back. Worn alone or layered, this is the piece people give when they mean something.

  • Adjustable chain
  • Also available in a boxed gift set

Hand-finished in Accra and presented in a Queen Dor's pouch.

Name: Gye Nyame Pendant Necklace
Short description: The most widely worn of all Adinkra symbols.
Description:
Gye Nyame — Except for God. Wear the reminder that nothing happens outside God's knowledge.

Worn as reassurance as much as declaration — a quiet reminder of what holds everything together.

  • Adjustable chain
  • Pairs with the Gye Nyame studs

Hand-finished in Accra and presented in a Queen Dor's pouch.

Name: Akoma Stud Earrings
Short description: Small, everyday, and the easiest first piece to give.
Description:
Akoma — The heart. For the days that ask for patience.

Akoma is the heart — patience, tolerance, endurance. A stud to wear on the days that ask for it.

  • Light enough for all-day wear

Hand-finished in Accra and presented in a Queen Dor's pouch.

Name: Bese Saka Adjustable Bracelet
Short description: One size, adjustable, and the natural partner to the Sankofa pendant.
Description:
Bese Saka — The sack of cola nuts. Abundance shared is abundance kept.

A sack of cola nuts stood for affluence and for the people who traded it. Abundance, and the responsibility that comes with it.

  • Stacks with the Adinkrahene set

Hand-finished in Accra and presented in a Queen Dor's pouch.

Nkyinkyim — The twisting. For the ones who change shape and keep going.
